name: The Four Bowls
region_detail: A broad sandstone hilltop near the transition from grasslands to uplands.
site_type: ceremonial ground | Ancient sites; inhabited locations | Ancestral Broadmaw feasting ground and seasonal gathering site.
history: Four enormous bowls were carved from separate boulders upon this hilltop long before Cadorian settlement. Broadmaw families regard the site as a customary gathering ground where offerings are deposited and disputes may be discussed under the hospitality of the host kindred. Its origins are preserved through oral tradition rather than written records.
current_state: The site is seldom occupied for long periods, though fresh cattle bones and trampled grass indicate a recent visit. A Broadmaw collector has begun demanding cattle from neighboring ranchsteads, and some of the demanded tribute may be brought to the bowls. The site remains important to kindreds unconnected with the collector.
inhabitants: Occasional Broadmaw families, travelers, and tribute collectors; carrion birds. No permanent garrison.
danger_level: Low while unoccupied; high when giants gather, particularly if their customs are violated.
points_of_interest:
Four immense stone bowls; hearths ringed with boulders; broad sitting stones; piles of offerings; weathered carved motifs; sheltered approach used by cattle driven uphill.

Unresolved elements: Who carved the bowls and what each originally represented.; Whether the tribute collector acts with Grudda's approval.; Whether the storm-walking pursuer described in the legend exists.; Which kindreds attend the next gathering and what obligations they recognize.
discovery: A broad sandstone hilltop near the transition from grasslands to uplands. Ranchers near the uplands report enormous footprints leading toward the hill. Broadmaw travelers can identify the feasting ground and explain its customary use.
